### 3. CLEAN & STANDARDIZE

```{r Clean and standardize key variables}
whaling_clean <- whaling_raw |>

  # Keep records from 1986 onward to match the post-moratorium study period
  filter(Year >= 1986) |>

  # Rename key variables so the analysis code is easier to read
  rename(
    year = Year,
    ocean = Oc,
    area = Area,
    expedition_code = Excode,
    nation = Nation,
    operation_type = Ty,
    total_catch = Total,
    total_lost = TotalLost
  ) |>

# Convert abbreviated operation codes into descriptive categories
mutate(
  operation_type = case_when(
    operation_type == "A"  ~ "Aboriginal",
    operation_type == "C"  ~ "Commercial",
    operation_type == "Co" ~ "Commercial",
    operation_type == "Cr" ~ "Commercial",
    operation_type == "I"  ~ "Illegal",
    operation_type == "S"  ~ "Special permit",
    operation_type == "S*" ~ "Special permit",
    operation_type == "U"  ~ "Unknown",
    operation_type == "-"  ~ "No catch",
    TRUE ~ operation_type
  )
) |>

# Remove records explicitly coded as having no catch
filter(operation_type != "No catch")
```

```{r Check cleaned operation categories}
count(whaling_clean, operation_type)
```

```{r Total catch by nation}
nation_summary <- whaling_clean |>

nation_summary
```

### 4. TIDY DATA

```{r Convert species columns into tidy format}

# Create a lookup vector to convert abbreviated species codes into readable names
species_lookup <- c(
  "TBlue" = "Blue Whale",
  "PBlue" = "Pygmy Blue Whale",
  "Fin"   = "Fin Whale",
  "Spm"   = "Sperm Whale",
  "Hbk"   = "Humpback Whale",
  "Sei"   = "Sei Whale",
  "Bryd"  = "Bryde's Whale",
  "Mi:C"  = "Common Minke Whale",
  "Mi:A"  = "Antarctic Minke Whale",
  "Gray"  = "Gray Whale",
  "Bhd"   = "Bowhead Whale",
  "Ri"    = "Right Whale",
  "Unsp"  = "Unspecified"
)

whaling_tidy <- whaling_clean |>

  # Convert the wide species columns into a tidy long-format structure
  pivot_longer(
    cols = TBlue:Unsp,
    names_to = "species",
    values_to = "catch"
  ) |>

  # Replace abbreviated species codes with descriptive names
  mutate(
    species = recode(species, !!!species_lookup)
  ) |>

  # Keep only rows representing an actual catch of that species
  filter(catch > 0)
```

```{r Inspect tidy dataset}
glimpse(whaling_tidy)
```

### 5. GEOGRAPHIC ANALYSIS

```{r Prepare geographic data for Google Earth Engine}

# Convert coordinate strings such as "70W" and "40N" into signed decimal degrees
convert_coord <- function(x) {
  
  value <- parse_number(x)
  direction <- str_extract(x, "[NSEW]")
  
  if_else(
    direction %in% c("S", "W"),
    -value,
    value
  )
}


# Clean the geographic lookup table and convert coordinate values
areas_clean <- areas_raw |>
  
  rename(
    ocean = Oc,
    area = Area,
    min_lat = MIN.lat,
    max_lat = MAX.lat,
    min_lon = MIN.lon,
    max_lon = MAX.lon
  ) |>
  
  mutate(
    min_lat = convert_coord(min_lat),
    max_lat = convert_coord(max_lat),
    min_lon = convert_coord(min_lon),
    max_lon = convert_coord(max_lon)
  )


# Calculate the total number of whales caught within each geographic area
area_summary <- whaling_clean |>
  
  group_by(ocean, area) |>
  
  summarise(
    total_catch = sum(total_catch, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# Calculate catch totals for each operation type within each geographic area
area_operation <- whaling_clean |>
  
  group_by(ocean, area, operation_type) |>
  
  summarise(
    operation_catch = sum(total_catch, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# Convert operation types into separate columns for each whaling area
area_operation_wide <- area_operation |>
  
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = operation_type,
    values_from = operation_catch,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  
  # Rename columns so they are simple to use later in Google Earth Engine
  rename(
    aboriginal_catch = Aboriginal,
    commercial_catch = Commercial,
    illegal_catch = Illegal,
    special_permit_catch = `Special permit`,
    unknown_catch = Unknown
  )
  
# Identify the operation type responsible for the largest catch in each area
area_dominant <- area_operation |>
  
  group_by(ocean, area) |>
  
  slice_max(
    order_by = operation_catch,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) |>
  
  ungroup() |>
  
  rename(
    dominant_operation = operation_type
  ) |>
  
  select(
    ocean,
    area,
    dominant_operation
  )


# Combine total catch, operation breakdown, dominant operation and geographic boundaries
whaling_gee <- area_summary |>
  
  left_join(
    area_operation_wide,
    by = c("ocean", "area")
  ) |>
  
  left_join(
    area_dominant,
    by = c("ocean", "area")
  ) |>
  
  left_join(
    areas_clean,
    by = c("ocean", "area")
  ) |>
  
  # Calculate the percentage contribution of each operation type
  mutate(
    aboriginal_pct = round((aboriginal_catch / total_catch) * 100, 1),
    commercial_pct = round((commercial_catch / total_catch) * 100, 1),
    illegal_pct = round((illegal_catch / total_catch) * 100, 1),
    special_permit_pct = round((special_permit_catch / total_catch) * 100, 1),
    unknown_pct = round((unknown_catch / total_catch) * 100, 1)
  ) |>
  
  # Arrange columns into a logical order for Google Earth Engine
  select(
    area,
    ocean,
    total_catch,
    dominant_operation,
    
    aboriginal_catch,
    aboriginal_pct,
    
    commercial_catch,
    commercial_pct,
    
    illegal_catch,
    illegal_pct,
    
    special_permit_catch,
    special_permit_pct,
    
    unknown_catch,
    unknown_pct,
    
    min_lat,
    max_lat,
    min_lon,
    max_lon
  )


# Inspect the completed dataset before exporting
whaling_gee
```

```{r Export geographic dataset for Google Earth Engine}

# Create an outputs folder if one does not already exist
dir.create(
  "outputs",
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

# Export the cleaned geographic summary as a CSV for Google Earth Engine
write_csv(
  whaling_gee,
  "outputs/whaling_areas_gee.csv"
)
```

### 6. DEMOGRAPHIC ANALYSIS

```{r Summarize catch by nation and operation type}

# Summarize cumulative catch for each nation and operation type
nation_operation_summary <- whaling_clean |>
  
  group_by(nation, operation_type) |>
  
  summarise(
    total_catch = sum(total_catch, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  
  # Calculate total catch for each nation so bars can be ordered by magnitude
  group_by(nation) |>
  
  mutate(
    nation_total = sum(total_catch)
  ) |>
  
  ungroup()

nation_operation_summary
```

```{r Plot catch by nation and operation type}

# Plot cumulative catch by nation, with operation type shown by color
ggplot(
  nation_operation_summary,
  aes(
    x = reorder(nation, nation_total),
    y = total_catch,
    fill = operation_type
  )
) +
  
  # Stack operation types to show the composition of each nation's total catch
  geom_col() +
  
  # Flip coordinates so nation names are easier to read
  coord_flip() +
  
  # Use the same operation-type colors as the Google Earth Engine map
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Aboriginal" = "#1B9E77",
      "Commercial" = "#D95F02",
      "Illegal" = "#000000",
      "Special permit" = "#7570B3",
      "Unknown" = "#FFD92F"
    )
  ) +
  
  # Format the catch axis with commas
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::comma,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  
  # Add figure labels
  labs(
    title = "Global Whale Catch by Nation and Operation Type",
    subtitle = "Cumulative reported catch, 1986–2024",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Total catch",
    fill = "Operation type"
  ) +
  
  # Apply a clean presentation theme
  theme_classic() +
  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

### 7. TEMPORAL ANALYSIS

```{r Summarize annual catch by operation type}

# Summarize total whale catch for each year and operation type
annual_operation_summary <- whaling_clean |>
  
  group_by(year, operation_type) |>
  
  summarise(
    total_catch = sum(total_catch, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# Calculate total catch across all operation types for each year
annual_total_summary <- whaling_clean |>
  
  group_by(year) |>
  
  summarise(
    annual_catch = sum(total_catch, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# Inspect the annual catch summaries
annual_operation_summary

annual_total_summary
```

```{r Plot temporal trends by operation type}

# Plot annual catch as separate trends for each operation type
ggplot(
  annual_operation_summary,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = total_catch,
    color = operation_type
  )
) +
  
  # Connect annual catches to show temporal trends
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  
  # Add subtle annual observations to give the trends more visual definition
  geom_point(
    size = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  
  # Use the same operation-type colors as the other figures
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Aboriginal" = "#1B9E77",
      "Commercial" = "#D95F02",
      "Illegal" = "#000000",
      "Special permit" = "#7570B3",
      "Unknown" = "#FFD92F"
    )
  ) +
  
  # Display years at regular intervals
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1986, 2024, by = 5),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.02))
  ) +
  
  # Format annual catch values with commas
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::comma,
    breaks = seq(0, 6000, by = 1000),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  
  # Add figure labels
  labs(
    title = "Global Whale Catch Through Time",
    subtitle = "Annual reported catch by operation type, 1986–2024",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Annual catch",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  
  # Use distinct x and y axes without background gridlines
  theme_classic() +
  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),
    
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 12,
      margin = margin(b = 12)
    ),
    
    # Place the legend beneath the figure
    legend.position = "bottom",
    
    # Keep legend categories on a single horizontal row
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10)
  ) +
  
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      nrow = 1,
      byrow = TRUE
    )
  )
```

```{r Summarize species catch by nation}
# Define the major whaling nations to include in the temporal comparison
major_nations <- c(
  "Japan",

  "Denmark",
  "USSR",
  "Russia",
  "United States",
  "Iceland",
  "Indonesia",
  "Korea",
  "Canada"
)

# Summarize cumulative catch for each species within each nation
nation_species_summary <- whaling_tidy |>
    
  # Retain the major whaling nations for a readable comparison
  filter(nation %in% major_nations) |>
  
  group_by(nation, species) |>
  
  summarise(
    total_catch = sum(catch, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  
  # Calculate total catch for each nation so bars can be ordered by magnitude
  group_by(nation) |>
  
  mutate(
    nation_total = sum(total_catch)
  ) |>
  
  ungroup()

nation_species_summary
```

### 10. SPECIES COMPOSITION BY NATION AND YEAR

```{r Summarize annual species catch by major nation}

# Define the major whaling nations to include in the temporal comparison
major_nations <- c(
  "Japan",
  "Norway",
  "Denmark",
  "USSR",
  "Russia",
  "United States",
  "Iceland",
  "Indonesia",
  "Korea",
  "Canada"
)


# Summarize annual species catch within each major nation
nation_species_year <- whaling_tidy |>
  
  # Retain the major whaling nations for a readable comparison
  filter(nation %in% major_nations) |>
  
  group_by(
    nation,
    year,
    species
  ) |>
  
  summarise(
    total_catch = sum(catch, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

nation_species_year
```

```{r Plot species composition through time by nation}

# Plot annual species composition separately for each major whaling nation
ggplot(
  nation_species_year,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = total_catch,
    fill = species
  )
) +
  
  # Stack species to show both annual catch and species composition
  geom_area() +
  
  # Create a separate temporal panel for each nation
  facet_wrap(
    ~ nation,
    ncol = 2,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  
  # Display years at regular intervals
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1986, 2024, by = 10)
  ) +
  
  # Format catch values with commas
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::comma,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  
  # Add figure labels
  labs(
    title = "Species Composition of Whale Catch Through Time",
    subtitle = "Major whaling nations, 1986–2024",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Annual catch",
    fill = "Species"
  ) +
  
  # Apply a clean presentation theme
  theme_classic() +
  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```
